frame: chair frame, mm: +X chair's right, +Y forward, +Z up, table top Z = 0
rule: value_mm is measured on the model between p1 and p2 (kind 'height': p1's z); file_value_mm is the parts file's own number; mirror true = drawn on the left twin with x -> -x; kind 'radius' has p1 = p2 = the corner and value 0 = sharp in the model

sources.guess: our guess: no photo or tape settles it

dimensions.name: Arm thickness, front end
dimensions.note: Outside face, straight up and down, about 1 1/4 in. back from the front tip. No photo sees the front end, so the model carries the line straight on.

dimensions.name: Rocker thickness, between the legs
dimensions.note: Across the rocker, outside face to inside face, about a foot in front of the back leg. The photos may read the eased corners short; one caliper reading settles it.

dimensions.name: Seat back edge between the slats: how round?
dimensions.file_key: design.top_arris at |x| 150; families.seat_top_back_edge (r >= 4-5 or roll-off; M13)
dimensions.note: Where the seat top meets its back face, between a side slat and the back leg. The model has a sharp corner; the photos hint at a round of 3/16 in. or more, or a top that rolls off. A coin held in the corner tells.

dimensions.name: Arm thickness, inside face, near the back leg
dimensions.note: Inside face (toward the seat), straight up and down. The photos see this face only from one angle; the left and right arms read differently.

dimensions.name: Arm thickness, inside face, near the front
dimensions.note: Inside face (toward the seat), straight up and down. The photos see this face only from one angle; the left and right arms read differently.

dimensions.name: Seat width across the front corners
dimensions.note: Outside to outside of the seat, just in front of the front legs, a little below the top. The left side traced 3 mm narrower than the model there; the right would not solve.

dimensions.name: Domino end on the front leg, long way
dimensions.note: The Domino's end where it shows on the outside of the front leg under the seat. The photos read 25-26 mm with the glue line; we took it as a 10 mm Festool Domino.

dimensions.name: Centre slat thickness
dimensions.note: Front face to back face, half way up. The photos only say 'about 10 mm'; it is the thickness of the bent lamination stack.

dimensions.name: Rocker tail tip: corner round, seen from above
dimensions.note: The model's tail tip is square. One photo reads its corners as rounds of about 2.8 mm (1/8 in.). A coin or a radius gauge tells.

dimensions.name: Arm top outside edge: how round?
dimensions.note: The arm's top outside corner. No photo shows it close enough; the model has it sharp.

dimensions.name: Crest rail height, back face
dimensions.note: Top edge to bottom edge on the back face, in the gap between the left slat and the centre slat. The tape (photo 1555) read 3 1/16 in.; the photos say less. A tape hooked over a rounded edge reads long.

dimensions.name: Centre slat width, just under the crest
dimensions.note: Across the centre slat about 5/8 in. below the crest. The tape (photo 1553) read 3 7/8 in.; the edge traces say a little wider.

dimensions.name: Left rocker, tail tip to front top corner
dimensions.note: Straight line, outside face, from the tip of the tail to the top corner of the front end. The model uses one shape for both rockers; this rocker's own photos say 1118.6 mm. It is also the one check on the scale of the whole model.

dimensions.name: Right rocker, tail tip to front top corner
dimensions.note: Straight line, outside face, from the tip of the tail to the top corner of the front end. The model uses one shape for both rockers; this rocker's own photos say 1112.3 mm. It is also the one check on the scale of the whole model.

dimensions.name: Seat side edge off the table, left, behind the front leg
dimensions.file_key: design.top_z_of_y at y 434 (fit beyond its valid y 110-400)
dimensions.note: Chair standing on the flat bench: bench top up to the top corner of the seat's side edge, just behind the front leg. The photos say the right side sits 3/16 in. lower than the left; the model uses the average.

dimensions.name: Seat side edge off the table, right, behind the front leg
dimensions.file_key: design.top_z_of_y at y 434 (fit beyond its valid y 110-400)
dimensions.note: Chair standing on the flat bench: bench top up to the top corner of the seat's side edge, just behind the front leg. The photos say the right side sits 3/16 in. lower than the left; the model uses the average.

dimensions.name: Rocker top edge off the table, front end
dimensions.file: parts/rocker_profile.json + parts/rocker_ends.json (top outline; HUB_HANDOFF.md M14 quotes the model value)
dimensions.note: Chair on the flat bench: bench top up to the rocker's top edge at the front top corner. The photos cannot fix the rocker's tilt better than about 1/8 in. over its length; both rockers, please.

dimensions.name: Rocker top edge off the table, near the tail
dimensions.file: parts/rocker_profile.json + parts/rocker_ends.json (top outline; HUB_HANDOFF.md M14 quotes the model value)
dimensions.note: Chair on the flat bench: bench top up to the rocker's top edge about 2 in. in from the tail tip. The photos cannot fix the rocker's tilt better than about 1/8 in. over its length; both rockers, please.

dimensions.name: Seat front edge thickness, beside the middle
dimensions.note: Straight up the front face, 3/8 in. to one side of the point in the middle of the seat front: bottom corner to the top of the rolled edge.

dimensions.name: Seat side edge thickness, half way back
dimensions.note: On the side of the seat half way between the legs, straight up: from the bottom corner of the under-bevel to the top corner.

dimensions.name: Top of the crest off the table, in the middle
dimensions.file_key: highest point of the crest at x 0 (key_points.top_centre_z is the REAR arris, 1078.5)
dimensions.note: Chair on the flat bench: bench top up to the highest point of the crest rail in the middle. The tallest number on the chair, and a check on the scale of the whole model.

dimensions.name: Seat front: depth of the hollow
dimensions.note: Lay a straightedge across the front of the seat touching the middle point and one front corner; this is the biggest gap to the seat's front edge in the hollow.

dimensions.name: Rocker thickness near the tail tip
dimensions.note: Across the rocker 5/8 to 1 in. from the tail tip. The tape (photo 1493) read 1 3/16 in.

dimensions.name: Back leg width, just below the crest
dimensions.file: parts/back_legs.json (via model params back_leg.width_across_mm) + tape IMG_1556
dimensions.note: Across the back leg, seen from behind, just under the crest rail. The tape (photo 1556) read 1 9/16 in.

dimensions.name: Front leg thickness, side to side, low down
dimensions.note: Across the front leg seen from the front, about 2 in. above the rocker. The tape (photo 1495) read 1 1/4 in. but could not tell the edge from its round.

dimensions.name: Crest length between the back legs
dimensions.note: The crest rail's visible length: inside face of one back leg to the other, along the back of the crest near its bottom.

dimensions.name: Side slat width, just under the crest
dimensions.note: Across one side slat, about 5/8 in. below the crest, seen from behind.

dimensions.name: Seat depth in the middle, back edge to front point
dimensions.file_key: design.top_arris (y, z) at x 0 to design.pommel_tip.y at top_of_roll_z (x 8); straight line
dimensions.note: Down the middle of the seat, from its back edge (between the slats) straight to the point at the front, tape held straight, not following the dish.

dimensions.name: Width across the arms, outside to outside
dimensions.note: The widest point of the chair: outside of one arm to the outside of the other.

questions.name: Side slats: turned or flat?
questions.note: Look down on the side slats. Are they flat across, like the model, or is each one turned so its outside edge comes forward (about 7 degrees at the seat, 3 1/2 at the top)?

left_out.name: Arm length
left_out.reason: The arm curves outward in plan, so a straight front-to-back line between two points on the arm does not follow it; arms_geom.json lengths.plan (463.9 mm) is measured along the curve. Check it against the arm template instead.
